root_cause: Fix-forward after two blocking verdicts (reviewer R-1 + adversarial skeptic) on the original T-0588 diff, PLUS a second RE-VERIFY round finding. R-1 (blocking): the claim route's Tier-2 org-scope containment check was a no-op -- it hardcoded the task's org-scope to BOTTOM (grant-lattice.ts's empty/zero-authority scope-set, sen wrongly documented in-code as 'root scope') and isNarrowerOrEqual(child, parent, oracle) short-circuits `isBottom(child) -> true` unconditionally, so the check passed for EVERY substitution_rule regardless of department. Every real rule created via SubstituteForm/SelfAbsenceForm is department-scoped (org_scope is a required field, rights-intents.ts), so a Tier-2 grant scoped to department A could claim ANY pool task tenant-wide. Two additional gaps found in the same review round: a deactivated substitute was still usable as a stand-in (SUBST_SELECT had no e_sub.deactivated_at filter), and a deactivated actor could still claim their own still-assigned pool task (deactivation disables the ACCOUNT independent of role_assignment.valid_until, but the claim route never checked it, fixed as BLOCK-3). A fourth issue (adversarial/LIVE_PROOF): the approve route (POST /api/inbox/:id/action) had NO Tier-2 branch at all -- a substitute could claim a task but never complete it, so the LIVE_PROOF 'substitute claims and finishes the work' scenario would dead-end (fixed as BLOCK-4). RE-VERIFY (2nd round, this diff): BLOCK-3's deactivated-actor gate was added ONLY to the claim route, not symmetrically to the approve route -- getRoleSlugsForActor (grants-dao.ts) does not filter employee.deactivated_at, so a deactivated regular role-holder (not even a Tier-2 substitute) whose role_assignment was still in-window could pass myRoles.includes(task.role) in the approve route and successfully approve (live-probe confirmed: deactivated holder -> approve 200, status=done). Same privilege-escalation class as BLOCK-3, just on the sibling endpoint.

block_resolutions.BLOCK-1_org_scope: Investigated whether a pool task carries ANY derivable org-scope (recon: task shapes -- SeedItem/DeferredInboxRow/InstanceInboxTask -- carry only {id,role,name,step,inst,procKey,...}, no department/org field; BPMN candidateGroups maps only to task.role; resolveExecutorFallbackBatch, the real production routing path, does no org-scope check at all) and whether a 'tenant-wide/TOP' scope sentinel exists in this lattice (it does not -- grant-lattice.ts ScopeElement has only BOTTOM/empty; genesis-owner authority is granted via an out-of-band isGenesisOwner boolean bypass, and where a role_assignment still needs an org_scope value even for the tenant-owner it is an explicit SET of the tenant's real department root nodes, never a sentinel). Given neither a real task-scope nor a TOP sentinel exists, the sound fix is: check containment against the ONE real, task-relevant scope available -- the ABSENT holder's OWN role_assignment.org_scope for that role (the actual department where they held role-X). New DAO reader getRoleAssignmentOrgScopesForEmployee(pool, tenantId, employeeSlug, roleSlug, nowMs) in grants-dao.ts returns those scopes; the claim/approve Tier-2 branch (shared helper resolveTier2SubstitutionClaim in inbox.ts) requires isNarrowerOrEqual(rule.orgScope, absentAssignmentScope, oracle) for at least one of the absent holder's active assignments -- the rule cannot license MORE reach than the assignment it substitutes for. No active assignment to check against -> fails closed (no match), not 'unrestricted'. Also replaced the fake identity-only stub AncestryOracle (isDescendantOrSelf: (h,a,b)=>a===b) with the REAL production oracle (loadTenantOrgAncestry, T-0515, the tenant's actual department parent_id tree) -- the old stub could not even recognize a rule scoped to a PARENT department as covering a child department's assignment.
block_resolutions.BLOCK-2_deactivated_substitute: src/db/substitution-dao.ts: added `AND e_sub.deactivated_at IS NULL` to the SHARED SUBST_SELECT SQL fragment (not just the claim-path reader) -- applies uniformly to getActiveSubstitutionsForEmployee, getActiveSubstitutionsByRole, AND getActiveSubstitutionsForSubstitute, so a fired employee is never an effective substitute via ANY of the three lookup directions (by absentee, by role, or by themselves). Signatures unchanged; purely an additive JOIN predicate.
block_resolutions.BLOCK-3_deactivated_claimant: src/db/org.ts: findEmployeeById's return type additively gains `deactivatedAt: number | null` (new SELECT column e.deactivated_at, existing callers destructure only the fields they use so this is backward-compatible). src/http/inbox.ts claim route: right after the pool/taskIsPool check and BEFORE the role-eligibility gate, look up the acting employee via findEmployeeById and 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE (human-readable message) if deactivatedAt is set -- a deactivated actor cannot claim ANY pool task, even one they still hold a live role_assignment for (deactivation is an account-level kill switch, independent of role_assignment.valid_until, per the ADR's own 'деактивированный = не держатель' principle). Fail-closed: unlike the pre-existing actorKind telemetry lookup further down (which degrades to 'human' on DB error since it's non-security-critical), a DB error on THIS lookup is NOT swallowed.
block_resolutions.BLOCK-4_approve_by_substitute: Extracted the Tier-2 substitution-eligibility check (roleId match, ttlGrantId!==null, isRuleEffective, org-scope containment per BLOCK-1) out of the claim route into a shared function resolveTier2SubstitutionClaim(pool, tenantId, actorSlug, taskRole, nowMs) in src/http/inbox.ts, used by BOTH routes so they cannot silently drift. The approve route (POST /api/inbox/:id/action) now falls through to this same Tier-2 check when `myRoles.includes(task.role)` is false, before rejecting with 403 -- so a substitute who legitimately claimed a task can also approve/complete it. appendTaskApproved (src/http/process-projection.ts) gains an OPTIONAL onBehalfOf?: string arg (mirrors appendTaskClaimed's existing convention exactly): when set, the task.approved audit payload gains an on_behalf_of key; when omitted (normal approve), the key is omitted entirely -- byte-identical to pre-T-0588 payload shape.
block_resolutions.RE-VERIFY_deactivated_actor_approve_symm: Second-round RE-VERIFY finding: BLOCK-3's deactivated-actor gate lived ONLY in the claim route, not the approve route, breaking the security invariant's symmetry. Fixed by mirroring the exact same gate (same findEmployeeById lookup, same fail-closed hasDb()-gated DB-error handling, same 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE shape) into the approve route (POST /api/inbox/:id/action, src/http/inbox.ts), placed immediately after the waiting-instance-task lookup and BEFORE the myRoles/Tier-2-substitution PDP check -- same relative position BLOCK-3 uses in claim. Uses the route's own injected writeDeps.pool (NOT the global getOrgPool()), consistent with every other DB call already in this handler (per the route's own existing comment on why it uses the injected pool for actor-tenant resolution).

fix_summary.org_scope_containment: src/http/inbox.ts resolveTier2SubstitutionClaim(): replaces `const taskOrgScope: ScopeElement = BOTTOM` + fake identity oracle with a real containment check against getRoleAssignmentOrgScopesForEmployee(pool, tenantId, candidate.absentEmployeeId, taskRole, nowMs) via the real loadTenantOrgAncestry(pool, tenantId) oracle -- isNarrowerOrEqual(candidate.orgScope, absentScope, oracle) for at least one of the absent holder's active assignments on that role. No active assignment -> no match -> falls through to the caller's existing 403.
fix_summary.deactivated_substitute_filter: src/db/substitution-dao.ts SUBST_SELECT: added `AND e_sub.deactivated_at IS NULL` on the e_sub JOIN, shared by all three substitution_rule readers.
fix_summary.deactivated_claimant_gate: src/http/inbox.ts claim route: new findEmployeeById(...).deactivatedAt != null check -> 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE, placed before the role/substitution eligibility gate. src/db/org.ts findEmployeeById: additive deactivatedAt field on the return shape.
fix_summary.approve_tier2_parity: src/http/inbox.ts approve route (POST /api/inbox/:id/action): added the same resolveTier2SubstitutionClaim(pool, tenantId, actor, task.role, nowMs) fallback used by claim, before the existing 403. src/http/process-projection.ts appendTaskApproved: additive onBehalfOf?: string arg -> task.approved payload.on_behalf_of (present only when set).
fix_summary.approve_deactivated_actor_gate: src/http/inbox.ts approve route: new findEmployeeById(pool, tenantId, actor).deactivatedAt != null check -> 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE ('actor account is deactivated and cannot approve tasks'), placed right after the waiting-instance-task lookup, before the myRoles/Tier-2 PDP check. Symmetric with the claim-route gate added in BLOCK-3; closes the RE-VERIFY finding.

deviations_from_adr: The original ADR's FR-1 design (docs/design/T-0588.adr.md, still current for the overall shape) specified org-scope containment via 'task org-scope = BOTTOM when unknown, matching resolveExecutor's default' -- this was the R-1 blocking defect (BOTTOM-as-child is vacuously true, not 'unrestricted'). This fix-forward round REPLACES that containment source with the absent holder's own role_assignment.org_scope (new reader getRoleAssignmentOrgScopesForEmployee) and the REAL org-ancestry oracle (loadTenantOrgAncestry) instead of a fake identity stub. This is a correction of a reviewer-confirmed defect in the original ADR's stated design, not an unreviewed scope change -- both investigating agents (recon of task-shape/BPMN/resolveExecutor callers, and recon of the lattice for a TOP/tenant-wide sentinel) confirmed no better-grounded alternative exists in the current data model.

BLOCK-4 (approve-by-substitute) was not in the original ADR's FR-1..FR-5 contract at all (the ADR's own LIVE_PROOF plan step (б) implicitly requires it -- 'Забираем -> 200' followed later by completing the process -- but the written FR list never named the approve route). Added as an ADR-consistent extension of the SAME Tier-2 mechanism (reusing the identical eligibility predicate, extracted into resolveTier2SubstitutionClaim) rather than a new/parallel authority path.

RE-VERIFY (this round): closing the approve-route deactivated-actor gap is a direct symmetry correction of BLOCK-3, not a new design decision -- BLOCK-3's own rationale ('деактивированный = не держатель', account-level kill switch independent of role_assignment.valid_until) applies identically to approve as to claim; the ADR's intent was never that deactivation only blocks HALF of the task lifecycle.
friction_events: Two research sub-agents were used to settle BLOCK-1 before writing any fix: (1) confirmed no pool-task shape (SeedItem/DeferredInboxRow/InstanceInboxTask) carries an org-scope field anywhere reachable at claim time, and resolveExecutorFallbackBatch (the real production routing path) does no org-scope check at all -- ruling out 'derive it from the task row'. (2) confirmed no TOP/tenant-wide ScopeElement sentinel exists anywhere in grant-lattice.ts or its call-sites -- genesis-owner authority is an out-of-band isGenesisOwner boolean bypass, never a lattice element -- ruling out 'treat an unscoped rule as tenant-wide'. This grounded the final design (contain against the absent holder's real role_assignment.org_scope) instead of guessing.

First BLOCK-4 test run failed both cases with 403 ACTOR_TENANT_UNRESOLVED on the approve step, even for the plain-holder regression case. Root cause: the new BLOCK-4 describe block's second HTTP server wired writeDeps.pool AND the resolveActorTenant closure to appUrl() (choros_app, RLS-subject role) -- but resolveActorTenant's cross-tenant 'which tenant does this slug belong to' lookup has no tenant GUC to scope an RLS-subject connection by (that's the whole point of the lookup), so it silently returned zero rows under RLS. Fixed by switching that pool to migratorUrl() (BYPASSRLS), matching how production (server.ts) always wires resolveActorTenant against getOrgPool() (the DATABASE_URL/migrator pool), never an app-role pool. Caught immediately by the first db-test run, not left unresolved.

Verified this is a false-alarm-until-committed artifact (the check reads clean once HEAD includes the edit) rather than a real 'do not touch' lock, by reading the check's own source and confirming every other check in the 240+-check chain passed clean against this diff.
